Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Canonical snapshot deltas

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

replay/delta provides a sparse XOR codec and a bounded snapshot cache over canonical bytes from replay/schema. Use it to send changes against an acknowledged snapshot baseline. It never compares compiler-layout padding.

The little-endian delta format contains a u16 run count, then sorted, non-overlapping (offset:u16, size:u16, XOR bytes) runs. Values are at most 65,535 bytes. Encode/decode preflight the complete operation before modifying output and allocate nothing. Dense changes can produce larger deltas; the sender then uses a full snapshot.

Cache owns fixed-size values keyed by nonzero stream-local snapshot IDs. cache_find returns borrowed bytes. Copy a promoted baseline if it must survive cache eviction. Clear history when the connection/checkpoint serial changes.

cache_note_prehashed avoids repeating a digest calculation. It is a trusted local optimization: its digest must have been computed over the exact supplied bytes. It does not validate a wire-provided hash. The networking receiver still computes and compares the reconstructed target digest before using this path. The cache owns its byte copy; duplicate IDs require the same digest and bytes.

The network runner promotes only ACKs matching a snapshot actually sent on the current connection generation and checkpoint serial. Receivers reconstruct into scratch, validate checksum/schema/game state, then cache and acknowledge. Missing baselines request a full snapshot without inventing state or resetting the game when normal simulation history remains available.

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_delta/run.sh
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_net/run.sh

Checksums detect compatibility/corruption issues; they do not authenticate peers or prove that a client simulated honestly. The session retains that responsibility.

Encoding keeps very short equal prefixes on the byte path, then skips equal eight-byte regions with explicitly unaligned, bounded loads. A differing word locates its first changed byte from the appropriate endian-dependent end. Differing runs keep their original byte boundaries and ordered XOR format. Complete preflight and failure-without-output-mutation remain in place. Native and executed WASM corpora compare the resulting bytes with the bytewise reference.

encode_bounded(base, target, dst, budget) emits the identical sparse format only if it fits both the budget and destination. It can stop scanning once the candidate is too large. Unlike encode, failure does not report the required size; output remains untouched. Output must not overlap either input.

encode_smallest(base, target, dst, workspace) chooses the smallest existing sparse or LZ4 encoding that fits, preferring sparse on a tie. A bounded tiny-sparse trial can rule out LZ4; otherwise LZ4 stays in its existing scratch stage while bounded sparse encoding attempts to beat it. A nil workspace selects sparse-only behavior. Failure leaves output unchanged, and success changes only the returned extent. Workspace/input/output aliasing is rejected. Selection adds no allocation or workspace bytes, changes no decoder or wire format, and retains exact chosen bytes. The network runner bounds the result so that a delta must beat the full snapshot.
